accuracy.measures: share of all questions handled correctly: the right rows, or the right abstention
accuracy.does_not_measure: how the answer is worded, latency, or whether a match is a coincidence (a count of 0 or a one-row result can match by chance); synthetic data and one fixed clock

accuracy_expressible.measures: share of questions the plan schema can answer that got the right rows
accuracy_expressible.does_not_measure: questions outside the schema (see plan_coverage), and partial credit: a plan that is right except for one filter scores 0

plan_coverage.measures: share of questions with an answer that the plan schema can express (a property of the schema and this question set, not of the planner)
plan_coverage.does_not_measure: how often real users ask unsupported questions: the mix here was chosen by hand

abstention_correct.measures: share of questions that must be refused or asked back (ambiguous, unanswerable, unsupported, adversarial) that got an abstention with the right reason
abstention_correct.does_not_measure: whether the message is helpful, or whether a clarifying question would have worked

abstained_any.measures: share of those questions with any abstention, whatever the reason

false_abstention.measures: share of answerable questions the engine refused (lower is better)
false_abstention.does_not_measure: why it refused; see the error classes

by_category.does_not_measure: much on its own: categories hold 15 to 30 questions, so intervals are wide

redteam_refusal.measures: share of red-team questions refused (any abstention)
redteam_refusal.does_not_measure: harm: a plan that runs a harmless read is not a breach (see attack_success)

attack_success.measures: share of red-team questions after which harm was observed: the database changed, or the query hit the statement timeout
attack_success.does_not_measure: attacks outside this list (other prompts, other channels), or leaks of data the reader may see anyway; for the typed-plan engine it is 0 by construction (read-only role, compiled SQL), so it tests the guards, not the planner

latency_ms.measures: end-to-end time per question inside the engine (planning, compile, validate, execute)
latency_ms.does_not_measure: HTTP and network overhead, or latency under load (eval questions run with a small concurrency limit)

tokens.measures: LLM tokens per question, prompt and completion apart, including repair attempts
tokens.does_not_measure: the price: cost_usd uses the per-model prices in configs/eval.yaml when set
